text: The role of humiliation/negative appraisal leading to a sense of inescapable entrapment in vulnerable individuals is a core feature of progression towards suicidality in the IMV model. We postulate that humiliation and shame may also play a role in intensifying thwarted belonging and perceived burdensomeness, leading to maladaptive coping which affects the two phases of acquired capability of suicidal desire and attempt in adolescence. What this means for adolescents and young adults is very relevant. In the context of negative life events, humiliation is the single most experienced life stress among adolescents followed by interpersonal loss [ 9 ], and thus warrants further attention. The process of ‘humiliation’ refers to two different forms of experience. Firstly; the act of humiliating or being humiliated, and secondly; the state or feeling of being humiliated. Essentially, humiliation can be considered as an external event or an internal state.
source_label: Associations between humiliation, shame, self-harm and suicidality among adolescents and young adults: A systematic review
